To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the density of zeros for a channel with uncorrelated taps is the same for the case of zero-mean and nonzero-mean taps, and that the density is a function of the ratio of the variance of the first tap and the variance of all other taps.

the zeros of mobile channel transfer functions are not randomly distributed, and that the zeros are not uniformly distributed in the unit circle, but rather they tend to be concentrated on the unit circle.
the zeros of the GSM/EDGE channel are distributed according to a density which is a function of the channel delay spread, the transmit pulse shape, and the receiver pulse shape.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) The statistical properties of the zeros of the discrete-time transfer function of mobile radio channels, (2) their application to the calculation of the performance of suboptimum equalizers, and (3) their implications for equalizer implementation.
the statistics of zeros of mobile channel impulse responses and their implications for the design of optimum and suboptimum equalizers.
the statistical properties of the zeros of the discrete-time transfer function of mobile channels, and the implications of these properties for the design of equalizers for ISI channels.

for a given channel model and a given channel estimation scheme the optimum equalizer can be designed using the statistical distributions of the zeros.

the zeros of mobile channel transfer functions are distributed in a way which makes the use of suboptimum equalization algorithms possible and which allows the use of a very small number of coefficients for the equalization.

the distribution of zeros in mobile channels is a powerful tool for the design of equalizers for ISI channels.

we have shown that the zeros of the overall channel transfer function are not distributed randomly but have a well-defined distribution, which can be exploited for the design of equalizers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the zeros of the overall impulse response of mobile channels are clustered around the unit circle in the complex plane, which implies that a simple zero-forcing equalizer is sufficient to achieve a low error probability.
